title: @fermi chat input not visible/usable
description:
What's broken: @fermi chat pane opens but has no visible input box or send button, making it impossible to interact with @fermi coach.

Expected: Chat pane should show input box with send button at bottom
Actual: Only shows welcome message, no input visible

Steps to reproduce:
1. Type @fermi in command input
2. Chat pane opens
3. No input box or send button visible at bottom

Console logs: No errors, input exists in DOM but styling makes it invisible

Root causes:
- Chat pane height too small (40%)
- Input box had very dark styling (invisible against dark bg)
- No send button styling (button existed but invisible)
- Old command input still visible (double input confusion)
notes:
Fix implemented and deployed to production.

Changes made:
1. Increased chat pane height from 40% to 50%
2. Made input box highly visible:
   - Lighter background (#3c3836)
   - Yellow border (2px, #fabd2f)
   - Larger font (16px)
   - Min height 44px
3. Added large yellow send button with → arrow:
   - Min size 60x44px
   - Yellow background with darker border
   - Large 24px arrow icon
4. Hid old command input when chat is open (no double input confusion)
5. Added explicit Enter key handler for web compatibility
6. Added console logging for debugging

Commits:
- dc29cc5: Make @fermi collapsed tab more visible
- 38a5dc9: Add logging and improve discoverability
- 5a35e44: Add send button and improve input handling
- fbbac7e: Make input visible and hide command input
- 8f6031a: Make input and send button highly visible

Pushed to master: 8f6031a

Verification steps:
1. Refresh browser (Ctrl+Shift+R for hard refresh)
2. Type @fermi in command input OR click yellow tab at bottom
3. Chat pane should open
4. Look at bottom of chat pane - should see:
   - Input box with YELLOW BORDER and gray background
   - Large YELLOW BUTTON with → arrow on the right
   - Yellow line separating input from chat messages
5. Type 'triangular' in input
6. Click → button or press Enter
7. Should see Fermi's response explaining triangular distribution

Expected: Input and button clearly visible, chat works

Ready for verification by human.

title: Configure Vercel KV environment variables
description:
The backend KV migration is complete but Vercel KV environment variables are not configured in production.

Error in console:
@vercel/kv: Missing required environment variables KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN

Steps to fix:
1. Go to Vercel dashboard: https://vercel.com/
2. Select uffp-backend project
3. Go to Storage tab
4. Create a new KV database (or connect existing)
5. Copy the environment variables
6. Go to Settings > Environment Variables
7. Add KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN
8. Redeploy

Impact: Blocks uffp_mobile-87u deployment
notes:
Final fix deployed - added ioredis adapter for Redis URLs with credentials.

@vercel/kv doesn't support URLs with embedded credentials (username:password in URL).
Created redis-client.ts adapter that uses ioredis for generic Redis URLs.

Verification steps:
1. Wait ~2 minutes for deployment
2. Refresh app at https://uffpmobile.vercel.app/
3. Create forecast: /question Will AMD reach 00 in 2025?
4. Console should show: 'Created forecast on backend' with ID
5. NO errors about credentials or KV

This should FINALLY work!

Ready for verification.
close_reason: Fixed: Configured ioredis adapter to handle REDIS_URL with embedded credentials. Backend now successfully persists forecasts to Redis.

title: Refactor to @fermi-as-CLI UX paradigm
description:
Current state: Mixed UX with old command input + @fermi chat causing confusion

Goal: @fermi chat becomes THE primary interface - a smart embedded CLI

Requirements:
1. Remove/minimize old command input (just 'Type @fermi to get started')
2. ALL commands work in @fermi chat:
   - /p, /dist, /direction, /save (driver config)
   - @agent_name (invoke agents)
   - /list, /question, /simulate (app commands)
   - /-h or /help - show all commands with descriptions & context
3. Hints appear as Fermi suggestions IN chat with click-to-execute:
   Example:
   User: 'I want to configure this driver'
   Fermi: 'I can help! Try:'
   [/p 10 50 90] (clickable) - Set parameters
   [/dist triangular] (clickable) - Set distribution  
4. Context-aware commands:
   - Commands for wrong context show error
   - Invalid commands ghost out/disabled
5. Collapsible chat pane (hide to interact with app visually)

Benefits:
- Single coherent UX paradigm
- Less confusion
- Contextual help built-in
- Click-to-execute convenience
- Smart CLI feel

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Old command input removed/minimized
- [ ] All commands work in @fermi
- [ ] /-h shows context-aware command list
- [ ] Hints clickable in chat
- [ ] Invalid commands handled gracefully
- [ ] Collapsible pane works smoothly
notes:
✅ @fermi-as-CLI refactor complete!

Implemented:
1. ✅ Command execution in @fermi chat (/-h, /question, /driver, /p, /dist, etc.)
2. ✅ Context detection (forecast_list, forecast_active, driver_config, etc.)
3. ✅ Clickable command suggestions (auto-execute or populate input)
4. ✅ State updates from commands (create forecasts, configure drivers, etc.)
5. ✅ Toned down styling (darker yellows, smaller sizes)
6. ✅ Hide old hints when fermi open
7. ✅ Fixed addFermiMessage function ordering

Commits:
- ca47274: Command registry system
- efe1ef2: Full integration with chat UI

Ready for verification. Test by:
1. Type @fermi to open chat
2. Type /-h to see all commands
3. Try /question Will AMD reach 00?
4. Click on suggested commands
5. See if commands execute properly

Expected: @fermi chat is now the primary interface with smart CLI

title: Cannot simulate local-only forecasts
description:
Old forecasts created with local-only IDs (e.g., 1769844910607) cannot be simulated because they don't exist on backend. Backend returns 404 when trying to simulate.

Possible solutions:
1. Add migration to push old local forecasts to backend
2. Add UI indicator showing which forecasts are local-only vs backend-synced  
3. Allow local-only simulation for forecasts without backend IDs
4. Add /migrate command to push current forecast to backend

Current workaround: Create new forecasts with /question after backend sync is enabled.

title: Backend using in-memory storage - data lost on restart
description:
CRITICAL: Backend database.ts uses in-memory Map storage which loses all data when Vercel serverless functions restart (which happens frequently).

Current code:
const forecasts = new Map<string, Forecast>();

This causes:
- Forecasts created successfully but lost minutes later
- 'Forecast not found' errors when adding drivers
- Complete data loss on each deployment

Solution: Migrate to persistent storage:
1. Vercel KV (Redis) - recommended for serverless
2. Vercel Postgres
3. Supabase
4. Any persistent database

Impact: P0 - blocks all backend functionality
notes:
Fix deployed to production.

Migrated from in-memory Map storage to Vercel KV (Redis) for persistent storage.

Verification steps:
1. Create a new forecast with /question
2. Check console - should see backend create logs
3. Wait 5 minutes (or trigger new deploy)
4. Add a driver to the forecast
5. Should NOT get 'Forecast not found' error

Expected: Forecasts persist across serverless function restarts and drivers can be added successfully.

Ready for verification by human.

title: Debug charts not rendering after simulation
description:
Charts don't appear after simulation runs successfully.

Console shows:
- Simulation #1 complete: 0.95 ✓
- Backend returns simulation data ✓
- But charts don't render ❌

Root cause: activeForecast.simulations array likely not being populated.

Backend returns simulation in response, but frontend may not be extracting the simulations array from the updated forecast object.

Check:
1. Does backend return forecast.simulations array?
2. Is mapBackendToLocal() mapping simulations field?
3. Is activeForecast being updated with simulations array?

Test case: Run simulation, check activeForecast.simulations in console.
